description: Curated negative treatment not visible in the citation network (legislative supersession, abrogation).

treatments.by: ADA Amendments Act of 2008, Pub. L. 110-325
treatments.note: Toyota Motor Mfg. v. Williams: the ADAAA rejected its demanding standard for 'substantially limits' and 'major life activities' (Pub. L. 110-325, sec. 2(b)(4)-(5)); see 42 U.S.C. 12102(4).

treatments.by: ADA Amendments Act of 2008, Pub. L. 110-325
treatments.note: Sutton v. United Air Lines: the ADAAA rejected its holding that mitigating measures are considered in deciding whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity (Pub. L. 110-325, sec. 2(b)(2); 42 U.S.C. 12102(4)(E)).

treatments.by: ADA Amendments Act of 2008, Pub. L. 110-325
treatments.note: Murphy v. United Parcel Service: companion to Sutton; its mitigating-measures analysis was rejected by the ADAAA (Pub. L. 110-325, sec. 2(b)(2); 42 U.S.C. 12102(4)(E)).

treatments.by: Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009, Pub. L. 111-2
treatments.note: Ledbetter v. Goodyear: the Act provides that the limitations period for pay discrimination runs from each paycheck or other payment affected by a discriminatory compensation decision (42 U.S.C. 2000e-5(e)(3)).

treatments.by: Civil Rights Act of 1991, Pub. L. 102-166
treatments.note: Wards Cove Packing v. Atonio: its allocation of the disparate-impact burden of proof was superseded by the Civil Rights Act of 1991 (42 U.S.C. 2000e-2(k)).
Price Waterhouse v. Hopkins: the 1991 Act codified the motivating-factor standard (2000e-2(m)) and replaced the same-decision complete defense with limited remedies (2000e-5(g)(2)(B)).

treatments.by: Burlington Northern & Santa Fe Railway Co. v. White, 548 U.S. 53 (2006)
treatments.note: Mattern v. Eastman Kodak: its 'ultimate employment decision' limit on actionable Title VII retaliation was abrogated by Burlington Northern v. White, which asks whether the action would dissuade a reasonable worker from making a charge of discrimination.

treatments.by: US Airways, Inc. v. Barnett, 535 U.S. 391 (2002)
treatments.note: Barnett v. U.S. Air (9th Cir. 2000) (en banc): the Supreme Court vacated the judgment and remanded, holding that a requested accommodation that conflicts with a seniority system is ordinarily unreasonable.
